name: Leo Brouwer
milestone_by_age_26: Appointed to teach composition at the Music Conservatory of Havana in 1961, having already composed notable works including Prelude (1956), Fugue (1959), and Etudes Simples (1960-61).
early_history_summary: Brouwer began classical guitar at age 13 in Havana, taught by Isaac Nicola (a student of Emilio Pujol). He gave his first public performance at 17 and began composing immediately, producing Prelude (1956) and Fugue (1959). He studied composition at Juilliard and Hartt College before returning to Cuba to teach at the Havana Conservatory by age 22.
family_context_summary: Born in Havana to a family with deep musical lineage: his grandmother was the sister of renowned composer Ernesto Lecuona. However, his parents divorced when he was very young, his mother died when he was 11, and the wealthy family refused to pay for music education. He was effectively orphaned and self-taught.
parent_family_domain_summary: His father was a doctor and amateur guitarist who encouraged his initial interest in guitar. His great-uncle Ernesto Lecuona was a famous Cuban composer, but the family refused to support Brouwer's musical education.
primary_early_advantage_tags: dedicated mentor, elite conservatory, orphan adversity, self-taught, musical lineage
evidence_summary: Brouwer was orphaned by age 11 and largely self-taught, learning by studying sheet music in Havana music stores. Despite his family's musical lineage (great-nephew of Ernesto Lecuona), the wealthy family refused to support his education. His key advantage was his teacher Isaac Nicola, a direct lineage from Tárrega through Pujol, and later his studies at Juilliard. By 22 he was teaching composition at the Havana Conservatory, and by 25 he had composed Elogio de la Danza (1964), one of the most important works in the guitar repertoire.
starting_point: Born in Havana, Cuba in 1939 to a family with a distinguished musical lineage (great-nephew of composer Ernesto Lecuona), but orphaned by age 11 and raised in poverty with no financial support from his wealthy family.
current_position: Resides in Valladolid, Spain at age 86; remains active as a composer with over 700 works; received the 2025 Ignacio Cervantes Medal from the Cuban Cultural Center of New York.

trajectory.event: Gave first public guitar performance and composed his first work, Prelude, showing early compositional talent.
Traveled to the United States to study composition at Juilliard School and Hartt College, expanding his musical education beyond Cuba.
Appointed to teach composition at the Music Conservatory of Havana, establishing his institutional role in Cuban musical life.
Composed Elogio de la Danza, arguably his most famous solo guitar work, premiered at UNEAC in Havana.
Played in the premiere of Hans Werner Henze's El Cimarrón in Berlin, marking his entry into the international avant-garde.
Awarded a DAAD scholarship to work as guest composer and lecturer at the Academy of Science and Arts of Berlin.
Appointed principal conductor of the Orquesta Sinfónica Nacional de Cuba.
Received the Ignacio Cervantes Medal from the Cuban Cultural Center of New York; continues composing from his residence in Spain.

name: Mustafa Barghouti
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Barghouti went to Moscow to study medicine in 1971 (age 17) and returned in 1978 (age 24). By age 26 he was completing his specialization at Maqased Hospital. His major achievements — founding PMRS, PNI — came decades later.
early_history_summary: Born in 1954 in Jerusalem, Barghouti grew up in Ramallah. His father was the municipal engineer for Al-Bireh. He was active as a student activist in the West Bank before going to Moscow in 1971 to study medicine, spending seven years there. He returned in 1978 to specialize in internal medicine and cardiology at Maqased Hospital in Jerusalem.
family_context_summary: Born in 1954 in Jerusalem to a Palestinian family from Deir Ghassaneh. Father was municipal engineer for Al-Bireh. Family was politically active — grandfather and great-uncle were jailed by the British during the Mandate. Grew up surrounded by internationalist, progressive literature.
parent_family_domain_summary: Family was deeply political with a history of activism under the British Mandate. Father was a municipal engineer. No specific medical or professional domain transfer documented.
evidence_summary: Barghouti was still in medical training by age 26, having spent seven years in Moscow and returned to specialize at Maqased Hospital. name: Anna Bessonova
milestone_by_age_26: Won bronze medal in the all-around at the 2001 World Rhythmic Gymnastics Championships in Madrid at age 17, establishing herself as one of the world's top rhythmic gymnasts.
early_history_summary: Born in Kyiv to a sporting family — father Vladimir Bessonov was a Dynamo Kyiv footballer and mother Viktoria was a two-time World champion group rhythmic gymnast. Bessonova began training at age 5 at the Deriugins School under legendary coaches Albina and Irina Deriugina. She was the youngest member of the Ukrainian team at the 1999 World Championships and won her first World Championship medal in 2001.
family_context_summary: Born into an elite sporting family in Kyiv: father was a professional footballer for Dynamo Kyiv, mother was a two-time World champion in group rhythmic gymnastics. Parents actively supported her training from age 5.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was a two-time World champion group rhythmic gymnast who introduced Anna to the sport and directed her to the Deriugins School. Father was a professional footballer for Dynamo Kyiv, providing an elite-athlete family environment.
primary_early_advantage_tags: family athletic lineage, elite gymnastics school, world-champion coaches, early specialization, prodigy
evidence_summary: Bessonova's path was shaped by deep family domain advantage — her mother was a world champion gymnast who channeled her into the elite Deriugins School at age 5. She trained under legendary coaches Albina and Irina Deriugina in Kyiv, the center of Ukrainian rhythmic gymnastics. By 14 she was competing internationally, and at 17 she won World Championship bronze, making her one of the most decorated gymnasts of her generation with Olympic medals in 2004 and 2008 and World gold in 2007.
starting_point: Born in 1984 in Kyiv to an elite sporting family: father a Dynamo Kyiv footballer, mother a two-time World champion rhythmic gymnast who directed her into the sport from age 5.
current_position: Runs a rhythmic gymnastics school in Miami, Florida; married Dmitry Momot in 2017; has two sons; largely retired from public life.

trajectory.event: Competed as the youngest member of the Ukrainian team at the World Championships in Osaka, Japan, gaining international notice.
Won bronze medal in the all-around at the World Rhythmic Gymnastics Championships, her first major international medal.
Won Olympic bronze medal in the individual all-around at the Athens Olympics.
Won gold in the all-around at the World Rhythmic Gymnastics Championships in Patras, Greece, becoming World champion.
Won her second Olympic bronze medal in the individual all-around at the Beijing Olympics.
Retired from competitive gymnastics after the Deriugina Cup in Kyiv.
Moved to the United States and married Dmitry Momot; subsequently founded a gymnastics school in Miami.

name: Rocky Johnson
milestone_by_age_26: Won the NWA Canadian Tag Team Championship with partner Don Leo Jonathan in April 1967 in Vancouver at age 22, his first major professional wrestling title.
early_history_summary: Born Wayde Douglas Bowles in 1944 in Amherst, Nova Scotia, Johnson left home at 13 and moved to Toronto at 16. He trained as a boxer, sparring with Muhammad Ali and George Foreman, before turning to professional wrestling. He trained at Jack Wentworth's gym in Hamilton, Ontario, and debuted in 1964. He won his first major championship, the NWA Canadian Tag Team titles, in 1967.
family_context_summary: Born in 1944 in Amherst, Nova Scotia, as a Black Nova Scotian descended from Black Loyalists and an African chief's son captured into slavery. His father died when he was young, and he left home at 13 after an altercation, becoming homeless before moving to Toronto at 16.
parent_family_domain_summary: No domain expertise transferred. Family background was one of hardship — father died when Rocky was young, and he left home at 13.
primary_early_advantage_tags: homeless at 13, self-made, boxing background, Black Nova Scotian, wrestling territory system
evidence_summary: Johnson's path was shaped by extreme adversity — homeless at 13, Black in 1950s Nova Scotia, self-reliant from adolescence. He found wrestling through Toronto's wrestling community, training at Jack Wentworth's gym and later Stu Hart's Dungeon in Calgary. His boxing background (sparring with Ali and Foreman) gave him physical talent. By 22 he had won his first major title, and he went on to become the first Black WWF Tag Team Champion in 1983.
starting_point: Born in 1944 in Amherst, Nova Scotia, as a Black Nova Scotian descended from Black Loyalists; father died when he was young, and he left home at 13 to live on his own in Toronto.
current_position: Died on January 15, 2020, at age 75 in Florida; final role was retired professional wrestler and WWE Hall of Famer (inducted 2008).

trajectory.event: Began professional wrestling career in Southern Ontario after training at Jack Wentworth's gym in Hamilton.
Won the NWA Canadian Tag Team Championship with Don Leo Jonathan in Vancouver, his first major title.
Won the WWF Tag Team Championship with Tony Atlas, becoming the first Black tag team champions in WWE history.
Inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame for his pioneering career as an African-American wrestler.
Died on January 15, 2020, in Florida at age 75.

name: Jacques Rogge
milestone_by_age_26: Competed in sailing at the 1968 Summer Olympics in Mexico City at age 26, representing Belgium in the Finn class; was also a multi-time Belgian national rugby champion by this age.
early_history_summary: Born in 1942 in Ghent, Belgium, Rogge was educated at the Jesuit Sint-Barbaracollege and the University of Ghent, where he trained as an orthopedic surgeon. He was a 16-time Belgian national champion in rugby and a yachting world champion. He competed in sailing at three Olympic Games (1968, 1972, 1976), with his first Olympic appearance at age 26.
family_context_summary: Born in 1942 in Ghent, Belgium, during the Nazi occupation. Father Charles Rogge was an engineer. Educated at the elite Jesuit private school Sint-Barbaracollege and the University of Ghent.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an engineer; no specific sports domain transfer documented, but the family supported elite education and multi-sport athletic development.
primary_early_advantage_tags: elite Jesuit education, multi-sport athlete, Olympic sailing, Belgian rugby champion, medical career
evidence_summary: Rogge benefited from an elite education at a Jesuit private school and the University of Ghent, which allowed him to pursue both medicine and high-level sports simultaneously. He was a 16-time Belgian national rugby champion and competed in Olympic sailing three times. His first Olympic appearance at age 26 in 1968 marks a material milestone. He later became IOC President (2001-2013), one of the most powerful positions in world sports.
starting_point: Born in 1942 in Ghent, Belgium, during the Nazi occupation; son of an engineer, educated at elite Jesuit private school Sint-Barbaracollege and the University of Ghent.
current_position: Died on August 29, 2021, at age 79 from Parkinson's disease; final role was honorary president of the IOC, a lifetime position he held from 2013 until his death.

trajectory.event: Competed in sailing at the Mexico City Olympics in the Finn class, his first of three Olympic appearances.
Competed in sailing at the Munich Olympics, achieving his best Olympic finish of 14th in the Finn class.
Competed in sailing at the Montreal Olympics, his third and final Olympic appearance as an athlete.
Became president of the Belgian Olympic and Interfederal Committee, beginning his sports administration career.
Elected as the eighth President of the International Olympic Committee, succeeding Juan Antonio Samaranch.
Stepped down as IOC President and was made honorary president for life.
Died on August 29, 2021, from Parkinson's disease in Ghent, Belgium.
